reason: Crossover #11: D002's 3-step answer_format (proven +21pp, n=20) composed with explicit rule-citation per reasoning step (new gene). The 94 'unknown' misses correlate with the model abandoning the rule system before deriving a contradiction. Forcing rule-citation in each step makes 'unknown' an outcome of explicit rule-trace exhaustion rather than a fallback after free-form narration loses its way.
directive: Crossover: D002's tight 3-step answer_format + new rule-trace constraint. BBEH problems explicitly state Rule1, Rule2, ... Rule20+ in the question prose. Variants MUST instruct the model to CITE A SPECIFIC RULE OR FACT in each of its 3 reasoning steps (e.g., 'Step 2: by Rule12, X follows from Y because Y was established in step 1'). If the model cannot cite a rule for a given step, that step should not be taken. Operational outcome: 'unknown' becomes the verdict ONLY when the model has explicitly enumerated the applicable rules and none derive the asked statement — not a give-up valve after long free-form reasoning. EVERY variant must compose the 3-step format gene + the rule-trace constraint. The conjecture under test: forcing explicit rule-citation reduces the dominant 'unknown'-cop-out failure (50% of family miss mass) by making the cost of saying 'unknown' visible (the model has to admit it found zero applicable rules).

l1_section_overrides_text.task_context: BBEH miss-pattern intelligence (n=298 measurements): 94 of 189 misses (50% of miss mass) are pred='unknown' when gt is proved/disproved. The model retreats to 'unknown' when free-form reasoning gets long — typical chain-of-thought outputs on misses are 1500-2500 tokens of narrative ending in 'we cannot conclude... therefore unknown'. BBEH is rule-heavy (questions enumerate Rule1...Rule20+ explicitly), so 'cite a rule per step' is operationally feasible and tractable. Hypothesis: anchoring each reasoning step to a named rule converts 'unknown' from a give-up valve into a derived outcome of explicit rule-exhaustion.
